clue.text: It might mean more travelling by train

definitions.text: It might mean more travelling by train

parts.words: It might mean more travelling by train
parts.note: reads like a note on longer journeys, but 'more' is about money: a rise in what passengers pay for a ticket

explanation.surface: A remark about something that would mean extra time spent on trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests more miles travelled; the real sense is that rail travel costs more.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in ticket prices means travelling by train costs more.

clue.text: Real fun turned out to be wrong for this ceremony

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase 'real fun' come out in the wrong order, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebration meant to be enjoyable proved quite unsuited to a solemn occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out to be wrong' rearranges REALFUN; 'for this' is a link pointing at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial service is a solemn ceremony held for the dead.

clue.text: Withdraw religious education pamphlet

parts.note: RE is the usual abbreviation for religious education, a school subject
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: An instruction to pull a leaflet about religious education from circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement is to withdraw it.

clue.text: Performing together

definitions.meaning: musicians on stage giving a live show
acting jointly, in unison with others

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both playing live on stage and acting jointly in agreement.

clue.text: Many a reformed set in class

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so it stands for many

indicators.note: the letters of 'a' and 'set' are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of people, once their group is reorganised, end up in a social class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges A and SET into ASTE, placed after C; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the traditional Hindu system.

clue.text: Noted clergyman is a builder

parts.note: E is a musical note, so a 'noted' clergyman is one with a note put before him
a rector is a parish clergyman in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A famous vicar turns out to be a construction worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' looks like 'famous' but is read as 'given a note': E, one of the musical notes A to G, goes before RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who erects or puts up structures is a builder.

clue.text: Singer given concession hurried round

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone
ran means hurried, moved quickly
O is round in shape, so stands for round

explanation.surface: A vocalist offered a small allowance rushed around.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest voice range.

clue.text: Caused a shocking death

parts.note: sounds like a lurid crime story, but 'shocking' is literal: death by electric current

explanation.surface: Someone brought about a scandalous killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' seems to mean scandalous; read literally it is an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing by an electric current is death by electric shock.

clue.text: Insane anti-revolutionary getting in most of the luck

indicators.note: one set of letters gets in among the others, so it is placed inside
only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped
the letters of 'anti' are thrown into revolution, that is, rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad opponent of revolution has been enjoying most of the good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-revolutionary' reads as a political opponent, but the hyphen hides fodder plus indicator: 'revolutionary' rearranges the word before it to NATI. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is a person thought to be mad, so used as an adjective it means crazy.

clue.text: Clear mess left by second small dog

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Clean up what a little puppy left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess left by' suggests the dog's mess, but 'mess' belongs to the definition and 'left by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear away mess or debris with a brush is to tidy by sweeping.

clue.text: Reserve added to a team

parts.note: to put on is to add, as in putting on weight
one stands for 'a', a single thing
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A reserve player joins a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside for later use is to keep it in reserve.

clue.text: Named but not known for sure

explanation.definitionFit: The word introduces a person named but not otherwise known, and also means confident or convinced.

clue.text: Old country passage

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tract is an area of land or country

explanation.surface: A stretch of land from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage taken from a book is an excerpt.

clue.text: Roof repairer on the way back struck another match

indicators.note: returning along the way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tiler lays and mends roof tiles

explanation.surface: A roofer returning home lit another match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit again, as a match or fire once more set alight.

clue.text: Duck below the bedcover

parts.note: an eider is a sea duck
down means below, lower down

explanation.surface: Take cover under the bed covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb meaning take cover; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with soft feathers is a bedcover.

clue.text: Utterly reckless, dangerous speed estimate

indicators.note: the letters of 'speed' are put in a dangerous, disordered state

parts.note: to rate is to estimate or assess

explanation.surface: A reckless guess at a perilously fast speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dangerous' rearranges SPEED into DESPE, followed by RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate acts are rash and reckless, done without regard to danger.

clue.text: Finishes what is endlessly intricate before a set back

indicators.note: the first part comes before the second in the answer
without its end, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: complex means intricate

indicators.note: set back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Concludes something which is very complicated ahead of a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops X from COMPLEX to give COMPLE; 'back' turns SET into TES. 'what is' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete something is to finish it.

clue.text: Indisposition from a meal is upsetting

indicators.note: the letters of 'a meal is' are upset, overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell after a meal that disagrees with you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like part of the surface verb but is fodder: A MEAL IS gives the seven letters. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A general feeling of being unwell is an indisposition.

clue.text: Arranges the salt you moved

indicators.note: the letters of 'salt you' are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the salt you shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out things is to arrange or display them.

clue.text: Bird not fully dressed?

parts.note: a dressed bird is prepared for cooking; read instead as someone wearing only a hat, a castrated cock with only headwear on

explanation.surface: A fowl that has not been completely prepared for the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CAP ON, the word describes someone wearing only a cap, hence not fully dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for eating.

clue.text: Doing nothing original

parts.note: sounds like idleness, but means producing only imitations of others' work

explanation.surface: Someone who is being entirely unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproducing another's work is imitating, with nothing original in it.

clue.text: Is tense

parts.note: sounds like a description of nerves, but grammatically the verb 'is' belongs to the tense of now

explanation.surface: Someone is feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective for anxiety; it is the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Is' is the current, now-time tense of the verb 'to be'.

clue.text: Agree a sound of amusement might be coming from the huntsman

definitions.text: might be coming from the huntsman

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond
ho, as in ho-ho, is a laugh

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a laugh might be heard from the hunting master.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry a fox hunter gives on sighting the quarry.

clue.text: The first mentioned topless shell

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: 'the former' is the first mentioned of two

explanation.surface: The first item named was a shell without its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes F from FORMER. An ormer is an edible shellfish found in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an abalone, a mollusc with an ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Not stopping to put into words

definitions.meaning: describing a fast train that makes no intermediate stops
to state or voice a thought

explanation.definitionFit: A non-stop train is a fast one; to voice or articulate thoughts is to state them.

clue.text: From idea that is incomplete somehow appearing like a god

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unknown order
the word is not complete, so its last letter is missing

explanation.surface: A notion that is only half formed somehow gives something a godlike look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts IDEA to IDE; 'somehow' rearranges FROM with IDE. 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Deiform means godlike, having the form of a deity.

clue.text: I look inside and find some flavouring

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to see is to look

explanation.surface: Someone peers in and discovers a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I look' reads as the speaker peering; it is fodder: the letter I with a synonym of 'look', both placed within the word 'and'. 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the seed of anise, used as a liquorice-like flavouring.

clue.text: It has a depressing effect on correspondence

definitions.text: It has a depressing effect on correspondence

parts.words: It has a depressing effect on correspondence
parts.note: sounds gloomy, but 'depressing' is literal: an object pressing down on papers

explanation.surface: Something that makes letter-writing a gloomy business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressing' seems to mean saddening but means pressing down, as an object holding papers flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperweight keeps letters on a desk pressed down.
